_comment: cc-P187: the web console's pages: every Shard Console tab and button, from the phone. One file, read by web-console/server.py (what each page shows, the inputs it passes, the checks before it runs) and by Get-WebPagePlan in scripts/Shard-Console.ps1 (the console action it runs, through the console's own Get-ActionFacts, Get-ActionPlan, Test-PlanSafety and Invoke-Plan). The Golem tab's buttons are web-console/golem-actions.json (cc-P182). action: a Shard Console action key (Get-ConsoleActions); art: Art.ps1's command (the Art tab). kind: read (changes nothing, runs at a tap), change, or dangerous (the LIVE shard, publishing, deploying, deleting, committing: a second confirm screen, and refused while another action runs); any button on the LIVE shard counts as dangerous. A change or dangerous button shows the console's plan first (a dry run of the same plan) and asks the console's own typed phrase when the plan has one (case ignored: phones capitalize). inputs: field names (fields below). locks: the Golem sign-up sheet resources it takes while it runs (D:/UO/golem/locks, owner Chase). minutes: how long it may run. answers: the lines its script's own 'Type yes' or word question gets on stdin, only after the second confirm. danger: the second confirm's plain words ({field} is the input). pcOnly: shown, greyed, with the reason, and refused. twins: every button and box of the Shard Console window (its Tag, else its Name) and its web counterpart: a button key here or in golem-actions.json, input:<field>, page:<what> (a part of the page that does it), logs:<source>, or pc:<the reason it stays on the PC>. scripts/tests/Shard-Console.Tests.ps1 fails when a console button has none (P187_EveryConsoleButtonHasAWebTwin). ASCII only.

force.label: Force: skip the quiet-window wait (not the DONE check, SYSTEM or the phrase)

vdFile.label: .vd file on the game PC (full path)

body.label: Body number (blank: a free one is proposed)

huesFile.label: The other hues.mul on the game PC (full path)

pages.title: Test shard
pages.caption: The throwaway test shard (sl-modernuo-test, port 2594, its own save). Rebuild is the only button that builds, through every test gate. Start fresh starts a NEW world with the live accounts copied in; Wipe test accounts (PC only) keeps the world.

buttons.label: Wipe test accounts (keep world)
buttons.pcOnly: it asks the new admin's password twice in its own window (Read-WipePassword), and a password never goes through a web page.

buttons.label: Rebuild through the gates and start
Open a client
buttons.pcOnly: it opens the game client on the game PC.

pages.title: Fix test shard
pages.caption: When the test shard will not start. Diagnose first: it reads the container, its health, its image and commit, and any crash. Restart, Roll back to last good, Rebuild a commit and Prune images each ask the console's phrase; none touches live.

pages.title: Shard question
pages.caption: What the picked shard is waiting on at its console, and one button per answer it takes. y and a delete account data (the save is backed up first).

buttons.label: Answer y (deletes)
buttons.danger: This answers y on the {shard} shard: it DELETES the data its question names, after backing up that save.

buttons.label: Answer a (deletes all)
buttons.danger: This answers a on the {shard} shard: it DELETES ALL the data its question names, after backing up that save.

pages.title: Snapshots
pages.caption: A snapshot is a copy of the Saves folder, accounts included. Creating or restoring one stops the container first if it runs and starts it again after. A restore snapshots the current save first (PRE-RESTORE). Nothing is deleted except a snapshot you delete here.

buttons.label: Restore selected
buttons.danger: This restores {snapshot} onto the {shard} shard: the current save is snapshotted first and moved aside.

buttons.label: Delete selected
buttons.danger: This DELETES the snapshot {snapshot} of the {shard} shard. It cannot be undone.

pages.title: World setup
pages.caption: In-game commands to paste into a client by hand: the console cannot run them, and cannot see whether this world has had them. Read from the code; only those that change a world are shown. Copy puts one on this phone's clipboard. Check which shard the client is on before you paste.

pages.title: Map and Art
pages.caption: Art checks run scripts/validate-art.py (read only). Check a .vd takes a .vd file on the game PC and a body number; Compare a hues.mul takes the other hues.mul. Exit 1 means it found problems to read, not that it failed. Map commands print the syntax of the six in-game map checks (GameMaster), typed in a client.

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.caption: Two read-only health checks; each writes one timestamped file (Logs: the newest diagnostic). The shard check reads the TEST container only. Disconnect VPN turns off a VPN that is making sl-ddns publish the wrong address.

pages.title: Commit
pages.caption: Runs D:/UO/Commit-ShardWork.ps1. Preview changes nothing. Commit and push asks for the phrase 'commit shard work': both repos are public on GitHub, so a pushed commit cannot be taken back. It waits for the quiet window and until every CC prompt has said DONE. While the Golem is awake it commits after each DONE by itself.

buttons.label: Commit and push
buttons.danger: This commits both repos and PUSHES them to GitHub, where they are public: a pushed commit cannot be taken back.

pages.title: Player package
pages.caption: Build package makes and checks a zip in player-package/dist and publishes nothing (refused while the shard repo has uncommitted changes). Publish selected is public: every launcher is offered it. Legion scripts: Publish to dev reaches only your own PCs.

buttons.label: Publish selected
buttons.danger: This PUBLISHES {packageZip} to get.shatteredlegacyuo.com and the website: every player's launcher is offered it at its next start. The publish script's own 'Type yes' is answered yes by this confirm.

buttons.label: Publish scripts to dev
buttons.danger: This publishes the Legion scripts repo to the dev channel on Haven, which only your PCs flagged dev read. Its own 'Type yes' is answered yes by this confirm.

buttons.label: Promote scripts to official
buttons.pcOnly: it asks which dev scripts to promote, then yes, in its own window; promote from the Shard Console.

buttons.label: Set up scripts repo
buttons.pcOnly: it asks where the clone lives in its own window, the first time; done once per PC.

buttons.label: Set up publish key
buttons.pcOnly: ssh-keygen asks a passphrase and Haven asks its password in its own window, and a secret never goes through a web page.

pages.title: Golem (more)
pages.caption: The Golem page has the Golem's buttons, the picker and the queue. These are the rest of the Golem tab.

buttons.label: Golem email setup
buttons.pcOnly: Setup-Email.ps1 asks the sender's app password in its own window, and a password never goes through a web page.

buttons.label: Move to the Golem
buttons.pcOnly: the one-time cutover from cc-autopilot (done: the Golem is active); Move-ToGolem.ps1 prints its dry run and asks again in its own window.

buttons.label: Golem settings
buttons.pcOnly: it opens settings.json in Notepad on the game PC to edit it.

buttons.label: Open Golem folder
buttons.pcOnly: it opens Explorer on the game PC.

pages.title: Websites
pages.caption: The websites in scripts/websites.json, on the game PC and on Haven. Pick a site: Open it here; for a game-PC site Restart, Redeploy or Logs; for a Haven site with an allowlisted deploy, Deploy to Haven (the phrase 'deploy to haven', then the deploy script's own word, which the second confirm answers). Each deploy keeps its log (Logs: the newest Haven deploy).

buttons.label: Deploy to Haven
buttons.danger: This deploys the {site} site to Haven with your own SSH key (its log is kept). Its deploy script's own typed word, if it asks one, is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Open NPM
buttons.pcOnly: it opens an SSH tunnel to Haven and the admin page in the game PC's browser.

buttons.label: Ops pages: deploy
buttons.pcOnly: on a first deploy it asks for the ops listener's token in its own window, and a secret never goes through a web page.

buttons.label: Ops pages: cut over
buttons.danger: This cuts the ops pages over to Haven: it stops the game PC's Play tests page, seeds Haven's data and switches the console and the commit to Haven. Its own word 'cut over' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Ops pages: roll back
buttons.danger: This rolls the ops pages back to the game PC: it takes Haven's data into testing and stops Haven's page. Its own word 'roll back' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Print queue: deploy
buttons.danger: This deploys the Sunflower print queue to Haven. Its own word 'deploy' is answered by this confirm; a first deploy that asks anything more stops there.

buttons.label: Print queue: roll back
buttons.danger: This takes the print queue back to the game PC and stops Haven's container. Its own word 'roll back' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Mega dashboard: deploy
buttons.danger: This puts the one Homepage on Haven and stops the stale one there and this PC's sl-dashboard. Its own word 'deploy' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Mega dashboard: roll back
buttons.danger: This stops the new Homepage and starts the stale one on Haven and this PC's sl-dashboard again. Its own word 'roll back' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Portainer (Haven): deploy
buttons.danger: This puts Portainer CE on Haven (its data volume is backed up first when it exists). Its own word 'deploy' is answered by this confirm.

buttons.label: Portainer (Haven): roll back
buttons.danger: This takes Portainer off Haven. Its own word 'roll back' is answered by this confirm.

pages.title: Art requests
pages.caption: Art requests from D:/UO/art/requests. Generate and Regenerate use Codex on your ChatGPT plan (or the API with your key and its monthly cap) and show the estimate first; results wait in review until you Approve, and Place puts them where they go.

buttons.label: Generate (API)
buttons.danger: This generates one image for {artId} with the OpenAI API, which costs money (the estimate above; the monthly cap still holds).

buttons.label: Import
buttons.pcOnly: it picks a picture file on the game PC (D:/UO/art-inbox).

buttons.label: Open review folder
buttons.pcOnly: it opens Explorer on the game PC; this page shows each request's newest picture.

pages.title: LIVE shard
pages.caption: LIVE: sl-modernuo, the real world save, real players. Every button asks the console's phrase and then a second confirm. Start, Stop and Restart act on the existing container only.

buttons.label: Start
buttons.danger: This STARTS the LIVE shard (sl-modernuo).

buttons.label: Stop
buttons.danger: This STOPS the LIVE shard (sl-modernuo): players are disconnected.

buttons.label: Restart
buttons.danger: This RESTARTS the LIVE shard (sl-modernuo): players are disconnected while it starts again.

buttons.label: Open a client
buttons.pcOnly: it opens the game client on the game PC.

twins.refresh: page:refresh (Refresh now, and every page re-reads its list when opened)
twins.autoRefresh: page:auto (the page reads the status every 5 s by itself)
twins.dryRun: page:preview (every change and dangerous button shows the console's plan, a dry run, before Run)
twins.test.tail: logs:shard (the last 2000 lines; following it live is the window's)
twins.worldCopy: page:copy (Copy puts the command on the phone's clipboard)
twins.worldTick: page:tick (ticks kept on this phone for the session)
twins.art.browsevd: pc:a file picker on the game PC; type the .vd file's path instead
twins.art.browsehues: pc:a file picker on the game PC; type the hues.mul's path instead
twins.diag.folder: logs:diag (the newest diagnostic file; Explorer is the window's)
twins.golem.queue: page:queue (the Golem page's queue; tap a prompt to read it)
twins.golem.openprompt: page:prompt (tap a queued prompt to read it)
twins.golem.opennotes: page:notes (tap a finished prompt to read its notes)
twins.web.open: page:link (each site opens from its row)
twins.web.check: page:refresh (the collector checks every site again)
twins.live.tail: logs:live (the last 2000 lines; following it live is the window's)
